title: SDK Rapid Adopter Funnel Playbook (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
A compact playbook for converting curious engineers into instrumented SDK adopters inside a single session (30–60m) or a short pilot (1–2 weeks). Focus: make the first integration fast, observable, and resilient, so product teams can validate value without lengthy infra work.

Primary outcomes (per funnel stage):
- Discover: link to 1-pager + 2 concrete example apps they can run in <5m.
- Try: local quickstart that runs with no cloud credentials (local emulation layer).
- Validate: telemetry + smoke tests that prove requests/latency/cost in CI.
- Pilot: sample infra example for canary and feature-flagged rollout.

Who this helps (personas):
- Frontend engineer (fast feedback, cares about latency and dev flow).
- Backend engineer (wants reliability, retry semantics).
- Platform/infra engineer (needs observability, cost visibility, rollout controls).
- Product manager (wants demo-ready success criteria).

High-level funnel and assets to attach: (minimal, copy+pasta for a workshop)
1) Awareness -> 1-pager + pre-read (1 minute).
2) Try -> repo: /examples/minimal-chat and /examples/qna; single Dockerfile + tiny script.
3) Instrument -> telemetry stub + CI smoke job.
4) Ship -> canary config + rollback doc.

Session blueprint (45 minutes in-person / remote lab)
- 0–5m: intro & outcomes (what success looks like).
- 5–15m: clone + run minimal-chat (we use local-mode so no cloud creds).
- 15–30m: add telemetry lines (2 facts): request_id and model_variant; run smoke CI job locally.
- 30–40m: wire fallback policy (local -> hosted); demo failover.
- 40–45m: next steps + commit checklist + owner assignment.

Quickstart checklist (developer-facing)
- [ ] Clone repo: gh.com/redwood/sdks/examples/minimal-adopter
- [ ] Install: pyenv -> python3.11, npm optional; run `make dev`
- [ ] Start local emulation: `./tools/local-server --stub` (no token needed)
- [ ] Run sample: `curl -s localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'`
- [ ] Confirm response and check telemetry log: `tail -f ./logs/dev.log` contains `request_id`
- [ ] Open CI smoke job: .github/workflows/smoke.yml, run locally with `act`

Repository layout (recommended minimal template)
- examples/minimal-adopter/
  - README.md (one-screen quick steps)
  - Dockerfile (single-step dev image)
  - src/ (tiny app wiring SDK)
  - tools/local-server (emulator binary script)
  - telemetry/spec.md (event names + minimal schema)
  - .github/workflows/smoke.yml

Telemetry contract (short):
- Events emitted per request: `request_start`, `request_end`, `request_error`
- Minimal fields required: `request_id`, `timestamp`, `model_name`, `model_variant`, `latency_ms`, `token_count`
- Example log line (plaintext JSON): {
  "event": "request_end",
  "request_id": "r_123",
  "model_name": "redwood-7b-v1",
  "model_variant": "quantized-x8",
  "latency_ms": 210,
  "token_count": 48
}
(Note: keep schema tiny to lower friction; richer properties optional)

CI smoke tests (pass/fail signals):
- Smoke must assert: non-500 response, latency < 2s for minimal prompt, telemetry event present (request_end).
- Use golden prompts to assert generation contains expected token subset (avoid exact-match fragile tests).

Rollout & gating for pilot (1–2 week):
- Canary: route 5% traffic to new SDK wiring (feature-flag). Monitor: error_rate, p50 latency, telemetry event rate.
- Gating thresholds: error_rate < 0.5%, p50 latency regression < +20% vs baseline, telemetry event success > 99%
- If threshold fails -> automatic rollback to previous feature-flag.

Failure modes and mitigation (short list):
- No telemetry emitted: fallback to verbose local logging + require dev to add `request_id` and re-run smoke.
- Token explosion cost spike: run with token limit in local quickstart; CI asserts token_count < 500.
- Network flakiness: demo failover path (local stub -> hosted) so UX remains stable.

Edge-case ideas (low priority experiments):
- Tiny browser-only quickstart (WASM shim) for frontend-first demos.
- VS Code devcontainer with pre-wired telemetry to reduce env friction.
- Short interactive prompt-builder UI so PMs can author quick validation prompts.

Open questions (we should decide before shipping templates):
- Do we commit to a single telemetry schema across SDKs or allow per-language extensions?
- Which CI runner image do we standardize on for smoke jobs (ubuntu-latest vs custom runner)?
- What is the minimum sample prompt/golden snippet set to make validations reliable across models?

Owners + next steps (90-day):
- Ava: consolidate examples into single repo and add `make dev` + devcontainer (2 weeks).
- Rahul: author .github/smoke.yml template and act docs (1 week).
- Sofia: telemetry/spec.md canonical draft & logging SDK helper (3 weeks).
- Marco: workshop slide deck + 30m lab script (1 week).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep friction <= 3 steps for the first run. Avoid handing off any cloud keys.
- Measure success: number of engineers who run the smoke job + open PR to adopt (goal: 10 PRs in first month).
- For demos, prefer deterministic short prompts; avoid adversarial open-ended ones.

Links to useful resources (workspace):
- Examples repo (placeholder): gh.com/redwood/sdks/examples/minimal-adopter
- Telemetry design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVX/Telemetry+minimum+contract
- Workshop slides template: drive.redwood.ai/sdks/workshop-template

Appendix: sample `smoke.yml` minimal (paste into examples):
- name: SDK smoke tests
  on: [pull_request]
  jobs:
    smoke:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Start emulator
          run: ./tools/local-server --stub &
        - name: Run smoke script
          run: ./tools/run-smoke.sh
  (we'll draft full file in repo)

End of sketch. This is intentionally compact — the aim is to make a reproducible 30–60m path that leads to a measurable pilot. Keep feedback coming.
